title: Complete Assyrian King List (All 116 Kings, Pruzsinszky), Remaining Sumerian King List Dynasties (Jacobsen AS 11) & Complete Babylonian Dynasties (L.W. King)

nodes.name: 1. Tudiya (1st Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.role: First King of Assyria (Ebla Treaty Attested!)
nodes.notes: First of the '17 kings who lived in tents' in the Assyrian King List; historically attested in the Ebla archives concluding a trade treaty with Vizier Ibrium of Ebla!

nodes.name: 2. Adamu (2nd Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.notes: Second king of Assyria in the AKL; earliest known historical ruler bearing the Semitic name Adamu ('Man/Red Earth'), cognate with Biblical Adam!

nodes.name: AKL Tent-Kings 3–8 Anchor (Yangi to Harsu)
nodes.notes: Anchor for Kings 3-8 of the AKL tent-dwellers, linked sequentially below.

nodes.name: AKL Tent-Kings 9–10 Anchor (Didanu & Hanu)
nodes.notes: Didanu corresponds to Tidnum/Ditanu; Hanu corresponds to the Middle Euphrates tribe of Hana.

nodes.name: AKL Tent-Kings 11–15 Anchor (Zuabu to Azarah)
nodes.notes: Kings 11-15 of the canonical Assyrian King List (Pruzsinszky Table 17a).

nodes.name: 16. Ushpia (Builder of the Temple of Ashur)
nodes.role: Founder of the E-hursag-kurkurra Temple of Ashur
nodes.notes: Credited in inscriptions of Shalmaneser I and Esarhaddon as the earliest founder of the great Temple of the god Ashur in Assur.

nodes.name: 17. Apiashal (Son of Ushpia — Bridge to Ancestors)
nodes.role: Last Tent-King & First of the 10 Ancestors
nodes.notes: Appears at both the end of Section 1 (17 tent-dwellers) and the beginning of Section 2 (10 kings whose fathers are known), linking Shamshi-Adad I's pedigree back to Ushpia!

nodes.name: AKL Section 2 Anchor (Kings 18–24: Hale to Yazkur-El)
nodes.role: Patrilineal Ancestors of Shamshi-Adad I Anchor
nodes.notes: Listed in reverse genealogical order ('PN1 son of PN2') in AKL Section 2 (Pruzsinszky pp. 48, 51).

nodes.name: AKL Kings 25–26 Anchor (Ilu-kabkabi & Aminu)
nodes.role: Amorite King of Ekallatum / Terqa Anchor
nodes.notes: Ilu-kabkabi fathered Aminu and the great conqueror Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 27–29 Anchor (Sulili, Kikia & Akia)
nodes.notes: Kikia built the city wall of Assur; Sulili (son of Aminu) marks Assur's independence after Ur III.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 30–32 Anchor (Puzur-Ashur I to Ilushuma)
nodes.role: Founders of the Old Assyrian Merchant Dynasty Anchor
nodes.notes: Ilushuma established free trade privileges for Akkadian merchants and founded the Old Assyrian trading empire.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 33–34 Anchor (Erishum I & Ikunum)
nodes.role: First King with Kultepe Eponym List Chronology Anchor
nodes.notes: Erishum I rebuilt the Ashur Temple and inaugurated the Kultepe Eponym List (KEL).

nodes.name: AKL Kings 35–38 Anchor (Sargon I to Erishum II)
nodes.role: Old Assyrian Anatolian Colony Trade Anchor
nodes.notes: Overthrown in 1808 BCE by Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: 39. King Shamshi-Adad I of Assyria (33 yrs, c. 1808–1776 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia (Contemporary of Hammurabi)
nodes.notes: Son of Ilu-kabkabi; conquered Assur, Mari, and Shubat-Enlil; father of Ishme-Dagan I and Yasmah-Adad.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 41–47 Anchor (Ashur-dugul & Six Usurpers to Adasi)
nodes.notes: Six claimants ruled briefly before Adasi founded the 1,000-year Adaside dynasty.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 48–53 Anchor (Belu-bani to Lullaya)
nodes.role: Early Adaside Kings of Assur Anchor
nodes.notes: Belu-bani (10 yrs) founded the unbroken Adaside royal dynasty; Bazaya ruled 28 years.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 54–66 Anchor (Kidin-Ninua to Ashur-nadin-ahhe I)
nodes.role: Late Old Assyrian / Mitanni Vassalage Anchor
nodes.notes: Preserved unbroken Adaside patrilineal continuity through the Mitanni era (Pruzsinszky Table 17b).

nodes.name: AKL Kings 67–72 Anchor (Enlil-nasir II to Eriba-Adad I)
nodes.role: Transition to Middle Assyrian Independence Anchor
nodes.notes: Eriba-Adad I (27 yrs) broke Mitanni supremacy, setting the stage for his son Ashur-uballit I.

nodes.name: 73. King Ashur-uballit I of Assyria (Amarna Letters EA 15–16, 1363–1328 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of the Middle Assyrian Great Power
nodes.notes: Son of Eriba-Adad I; wrote to Pharaoh Akhenaten as 'Great King' (EA 15-16) and married his daughter Muballitat-Sherua to Kassite King Burna-Buriash II of Babylon.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 77–78 Anchor (Shalmaneser I & Tukulti-Ninurta I)
nodes.role: Peak of the Middle Assyrian Empire Anchor
nodes.notes: Shalmaneser I founded Kalhu (Nimrud); Tukulti-Ninurta I captured Kassite Babylon.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 79–86 Anchor (Ashur-nadin-apli to Ashur-resh-ishi I)
nodes.role: Bronze Age Collapse Survival & Revival Anchor
nodes.notes: Ninurta-apil-Ekur restored dynastic stability; Ashur-dan I ruled 46 years.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 87–97 Anchor (Tiglath-Pileser I to Tiglath-Pileser II)
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser I marched to the Mediterranean and compiled the Middle Assyrian Laws.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 98–101 Anchor (Ashur-dan II to Ashurnasirpal II)
nodes.role: Founders of the Neo-Assyrian Empire Anchor
nodes.notes: Adad-nirari II inaugurated the unbroken Eponym Canon; Ashurnasirpal II built Nimrud.

nodes.name: 102. Shalmaneser III (35 yrs — Black Obelisk of Jehu & Battle of Qarqar!)
nodes.role: First Assyrian King Explicitly Naming Israelite Kings Ahab & Jehu
nodes.notes: Fought King Ahab of Israel & Hadadezer of Damascus at Qarqar (853 BCE); his Black Obelisk depicts King Jehu of Israel ('son of Omri') bowing in tribute — the ONLY contemporary depiction of an Israelite king!

nodes.name: AKL Kings 103–104 Anchor (Shamshi-Adad V, Semiramis & Adad-nirari III)
nodes.notes: Shammuramat served as regent alongside her son Adad-nirari III.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 105–107 Anchor (Shalmaneser IV to Ashur-nirari V)
nodes.notes: Assyrian Eponym List records the June 15, 763 BCE total solar eclipse under Ashur-dan III.

nodes.name: AKL Kings 108–109 Anchor (Tiglath-Pileser III / Pul & Shalmaneser V)
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser III ('Pul', 2 Kgs 15:19) and son Shalmaneser V (siege of Samaria).

nodes.name: Sargonid Dynasty Anchor (Sargon II to Ashur-uballit II)
nodes.role: Final Imperial Dynasty of Nineveh Anchor
nodes.notes: Sargon II, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon, Ashurbanipal, Ashur-etil-ilani, Sin-shar-ishkun, Ashur-uballit II — unrolled person-by-person below.

nodes.name: Ur I Dynasty: Mesannepada → Aannepada → Meskiagnunna → Elulu → Balulu
nodes.era: c. 2560-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iii-iv, Jacobsen pp. 93-95)
nodes.role: First Dynasty of Ur (Royal Tombs of Ur Era)
nodes.notes: 5 kings (177 yrs): Mesannepada -> son Aannepada (restored from Tummal Chronicle & inscriptions!) -> Meskiagnunna -> Elulu -> Balulu.

nodes.name: Awan (3 Kings), Kish II (8 Kings) & Hamazi (King Hatanish)
nodes.era: c. 2500-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iv, Jacobsen pp. 95-99)
nodes.role: Early Dynastic Hegemonies of Elam, Kish & Zagros
nodes.notes: Awan (Elamite dynasty, 3 kings), Kish II (8 kings incl. Kalbum son of Magalgalla), and Hamazi (King Hatanish).

nodes.name: Uruk II (Enshakushanna), Ur II (Kaku), Adab (Lugal-annemundu) & Mari (Ansud)
nodes.era: c. 2450-2350 BCE (SKL Col. iv-v, Jacobsen pp. 100-103)
nodes.notes: Enshakushanna of Uruk; Lugal-kinishe-dudu & son Lugal-kisal-si; Lugal-annemundu of Adab; Ansud of Mari.

nodes.name: Queen Ku-Baba (Kish III — Sole Female Monarch in the Sumerian King List!)
nodes.era: c. 2400 BCE (SKL Col. v 36-41, Jacobsen pp. 104-105)
nodes.role: Tavern-Keeper Who Consolidated Kish & Founded Kish III–IV
nodes.notes: Ku(g)-Baba ('Baba-ellit', reigned 100 yrs) is the ONLY woman listed as sovereign king in the entire Sumerian King List; mother of Puzur-Sin & grandmother of Ur-Zababa!

nodes.name: Akshak (6 Kings) & Kish IV (Puzur-Sin → Ur-Zababa → Nannia)
nodes.era: c. 2400-2334 BCE (SKL Col. v-vi, Jacobsen pp. 106-111)
nodes.role: Dynasty of Ku-Baba's Descendants & Master of Young Sargon
nodes.notes: Ku-Baba's son Puzur-Sin -> son Ur-Zababa of Kish, whose royal cupbearer was Sargon of Akkad.

nodes.name: Uruk III: King Lugal-zagesi (25 yrs — First Unifier of Sumer Before Sargon)
nodes.era: c. 2359-2335 BCE (SKL Col. vi 24-27, Jacobsen pp. 110-111)
nodes.role: Ensi of Umma & Sole King of Uruk III
nodes.notes: United all of Sumer from the Lower Sea to the Upper Sea before being defeated by Sargon of Akkad.

nodes.name: Late Akkad Interregnum (Igigi, Nanum, Imi, Elulu) → Dudu → Shu-Durul
nodes.era: c. 2193-2154 BCE (SKL Col. vii 1-12, Jacobsen pp. 114-115)
nodes.role: Final Rulers of the Sargonic Akkadian Empire
nodes.notes: 'Who was king? Who was not king?' Four rival claimants before Dudu (21 yrs) and his son Shu-Durul (15 yrs).

nodes.name: Uruk IV → 21 Gutian Kings → Uruk V (Utu-hegal) Anchor
nodes.era: c. 2154-2112 BCE (SKL Col. vii-viii, Jacobsen pp. 114-123)
nodes.notes: 21 Gutian rulers from the Zagros mountains expelled by Utu-hegal of Uruk V — unrolled person-by-person below.

nodes.name: Independent Lagash II: Ur-Nanshe → Eannatum → Urukagina → Gudea of Lagash
nodes.notes: Ur-Nanshe, Eannatum, law-reformer Urukagina, and pious Ensi Gudea of Lagash.

nodes.name: Isin I Dynasty Anchor (15 Kings: Ishbi-Erra to Damiq-ilishu)
nodes.era: c. 2017-1794 BCE (SKL Col. viii 23-45, Jacobsen pp. 124-127)
nodes.role: Final Dynasty of the Sumerian King List Anchor
nodes.notes: 15 kings of Isin I (Ishbi-Erra through Damiq-ilishu) unrolled person-by-person below.

nodes.name: Babylon I Amorite Dynasty Anchor (Sumu-abum to Samsu-ditana)
nodes.role: Complete Old Babylonian Amorite Dynasty Anchor
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: All 11 Amorite kings of Babylon I chained father-to-son below.

nodes.name: Babylon II First Sealand Dynasty Anchor (Iluma-ilu to Ea-gamil)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: All 11 kings of the 1st Sealand Dynasty chained sequentially below.

nodes.name: Babylon III Kassite Dynasty Anchor (Gandash to Meli-Shipak)
nodes.role: Longest-Reigning Dynasty in Babylonian History Anchor
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Kassite kings from Gandash through Burna-Buriash II & Meli-Shipak chained below.

nodes.name: Babylon IV (Isin II): Nebuchadnezzar I → Enlil-nadin-apli → Marduk-nadin-ahhe → Adad-apla-iddina
nodes.role: Revival of Native Babylon & Recovery of Marduk from Elam
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nebuchadnezzar I sacked Susa in Elam and restored Marduk to Babylon; Adad-apla-iddina married his daughter to Assyrian King Ashur-bel-kala.

nodes.name: Babylon V–IX: 2nd Sealand, Bazi Dynasty, Nabonassar (747 BCE Era!) & Merodach-Baladan II
nodes.era: 1025-626 BCE (L.W. King Vol. I pp. 184-208; Eusebius)
nodes.role: Ptolemaic Astronomical Era of Nabonassar & Chaldean Resistance
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: King Nabonassar (747 BCE) inaugurated Ptolemy's Almagest Canon; Merodach-Baladan II sent envoys to King Hezekiah of Judah (2 Kgs 20:12).

nodes.name: Babylon X Neo-Babylonian / Chaldean Empire Anchor (Nabopolassar to Belshazzar)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nabopolassar -> Nebuchadnezzar II -> Amel-Marduk -> Neriglissar -> Labashi-Marduk -> Nabonidus & Belshazzar unrolled below.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Belshazzar (Son & Coregent of Nabonidus, Daniel 5)
nodes.role: Babylonian Crown Prince at the Fall of Babylon
nodes.notes: Coregent of Babylon under Nabonidus until the city fell to Cyrus the Great in 539 BCE.
